chunks: Al-Husayn from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Rifah ibn Musa from Isma'il ibn Jabr said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) until we reached the time between the two evening prayers (Maghrib and 'Isha). He said, 'O Isma'il, proceed with the baggage and dependents until I catch up with you.' This was at sunset. I disliked leaving them to dismount and pray, while he had ordered me to stay with them, so I continued walking. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) caught up with me and said, 'O Isma'il, have you prayed Maghrib?' I said, 'No.' So he dismounted from his mount, called the Adhan, established the Iqamah, and prayed Maghrib, and I prayed with him. The distance from the place where I parted from him to the place where he caught up with me was six miles.

key_terms.بَيْنَ اَلْعِشَاءَيْنِ: Between the two evening prayers (Maghrib and 'Isha)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instruct his companion to do regarding prayer and baggage during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of *Qasr* (shortened prayer) and the flexibility of the Imam during travel, specifically highlighting the permissibility of praying Maghrib at its early time (*Awwal al-Waqt*) while continuing the journey. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates scholarly precision by ensuring the prayer was performed correctly before rejoining the group, emphasizing that the safety of the dependents did not necessitate delaying the obligatory prayer beyond its proper time. This incident serves as a key reference for jurists discussing the timing of Maghrib in relation to sunset and the conditions under which a traveler may separate from their group for worship.
